corners-floor-left: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent sprite atlas, square 1536x1536, STRICT 4 columns x 4 rows, 16 equally sized cells of 384x384 with at least 30px completely transparent gutters inside each cell. Sixteen isolated rock/root CORNER JOIN patches for a side-view mushroom forest metroidvania. FLOOR meeting a LEFT wall. Top two rows: OUTER corner, solid rock occupies LOWER RIGHT quadrant, horizontal walkable top extends RIGHT and exposed vertical face extends DOWN. Bottom two rows: INNER corner, open air occupies UPPER RIGHT quadrant, vertical wall extends UP on left and walkable floor extends RIGHT below. Every cell's actual 90-degree terrain junction is at the CELL CENTER (192,192), and its material arms extend about 140px from that center. Top eight cells are eight distinct OUTER/convex corner variants; bottom eight cells are eight distinct INNER/concave corner variants. Keep the exact required orientations consistently in every cell; do not rotate individual variants. Each patch should elegantly bend strata and twisted roots around the corner, rounding the sharp junction. Eight motifs per corner type: braided roots, fractured slate, clinging moss, pale fungal threads, small cyan shelf fungi, embedded ancient masonry, fine hanging rootlets, mineral-veined rock. Detailed realistic painted wet bark and rock, matching neon illustrated fantasy game terrain: midnight navy and BLUE-VIOLET stones, indigo roots, turquoise moss, restrained luminous cyan fungal accents, cool atmospheric lighting. Never brown or yellow-green. These are soft-edged material PATCHES that merge into existing cave surfaces, NOT floating islands, framed L-shaped blocks, stairs, dioramas, architecture, or complete scenes. Material fades naturally to transparent toward patch ends and the deep interior, exposed corner rim remains crisp. Genuinely transparent alpha background, no grid lines, labels, text, shadows outside sprites, or scenery. All sixteen patches clearly separated, no roots may cross cell boundaries.

attachments: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite atlas, square 1536x1536, STRICT 4x4 equal grid, sixteen EXTREMELY MINIMAL, QUIET cave attachments. Each sparse little object fits in the central 180x180 pixels of its 384x384 cell, at least100px transparent margin. Top eight cells: wall attachments, mount on LEFT and extend slightly RIGHT: two fine root strands; a tiny tuft of three moss leaves; one small dark shelf fungus; a sparse three-leaf fern; a short thin root loop; a little wisp of pale fungal thread; two small drooping leaves; a tiny patch of clinging blue-green lichen. Bottom eight cells: ceiling attachments, hanging DOWN from TOP: two loose thin rootlets; a short moss tassel; three fine fungal threads; a single delicate branching root; two tiny hanging leaves; a small dull indigo seed husk on a thread; a short tangle of three wispy roots; a small sparse web fragment. Mood subtle, unobtrusive, natural, barely noticeable environmental detail for neon mushroom forest platformer. Colors very DARK navy, muted indigo, desaturated deep teal, occasional restrained pale blue tip. Detailed organic materials but simple readable silhouettes. NO luminous cores, NO bright cyan, NO halos, NO neon emission, no crystals, lanterns, faces, skulls, shrines, big mushrooms, large cocoons, stone blocks, thick rock backing or rich ornate objects. Absolutely no big decorative clusters. Thin sparse forms. Genuine transparent alpha outside each object, no scenery, ground, captions, grid lines, or background. Keep every object and all alpha inside its cell.
